exposure: timing of planned birth (37+0 to >=41+0 weeks gestation)
method of planned birth (scheduled caesarean section, induction of labor)
cohort: Term singleton infants with birthweight >75th centile born in Queensland, Australia between January 2000 and December 2021.
finding: Scheduled caesarean section between 39(+0)-39(+6) weeks for large infants was associated with lower odds of severe adverse maternal outcomes, severe neonatal neurological morbidity, and other severe neonatal morbidity compared to induction of labor at 38(+0)-38(+6) weeks.
mod_finding: Scheduled caesarean section between 39(+0)-39(+6) weeks showed lower odds of several adverse outcomes compared to induction of labor at 38(+0)-38(+6) weeks, and for those undergoing induction, the odds of emergency caesarean section were lowest at 39(+0)-39(+6) weeks.
followup_time: up to 28 days post-birth for neonatal outcomes
